method_card.title: Holidays and Travel Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers holiday vocabulary, country prepositions and the near future tense for talking about travel plans.

FrenchEnglish
les vacancesholidays
au bord de la merat the seaside
à la montagnein the mountains
à la campagnein the countryside
à l'étrangerabroad
en avionby plane
en voitureby car
en trainby train
à véloby bike
à piedon foot
faire du tourismeto go sightseeing
bronzer sur la plageto sunbathe on the beach
faire du skito go skiing

Country prepositions: en + feminine country (en France, en Espagne), au + masculine country (au Canada, au Maroc), aux + plural country (aux États-Unis), à + city (à Paris).

Near future tense (le futur proche): Present tense of aller + infinitive. je vais, tu vas, il/elle/on va, nous allons, vous allez, ils/elles vont + infinitive.

Model: L'été prochain, je vais aller en Espagne avec ma famille. Nous allons voyager en avion et rester dans un hôtel au bord de la mer. Ce sera fantastique! (Next summer, I am going to go to Spain with my family. We are going to travel by plane and stay in a hotel by the seaside. It will be fantastic!)
steps: Learn key holiday, destination and transport vocabulary
Master country prepositions: en (feminine), au (masculine), aux (plural), à (cities)
Form the near future tense with aller + infinitive for all persons
Practice writing about future holiday plans using time phrases and opinions

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — appears in every exam series

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'L'été prochain, nous allons aller en Italie en avion.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence into chunks: L'été prochain | nous allons aller | en Italie | en avion.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: L'été prochain = Next summer. nous allons aller = we are going to go (near future: allons + aller).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: en Italie = to Italy (en because l'Italie is feminine). en avion = by plane.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Next summer, we are going to go to Italy by plane.

worked_examples.question: How do you choose the correct preposition before a country?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Check the gender of the country. Most countries ending in -e are feminine (la France, l'Espagne, l'Italie).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Feminine → en (en France). Masculine → au (au Canada). Plural → aux (aux États-Unis). Cities → à (à Paris).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Watch for exceptions: le Mexique ends in -e but is masculine → au Mexique.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Check gender: en (feminine), au (masculine), aux (plural), à (cities). Remember le Mexique is an exception.

worked_examples.question: Translate to French: 'Next year, I am going to travel to Canada by plane with my friends.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Identify the tense: 'am going to travel' = near future → je vais voyager.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: 'to Canada' — le Canada is masculine → au Canada. 'by plane' → en avion.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: 'Next year' = L'année prochaine. 'with my friends' = avec mes amis.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: L'année prochaine, je vais voyager au Canada en avion avec mes amis.

Complete the sentence with the correct form of aller

gaps.rule: Near future — je form of aller
gaps.correct_explain: vais is the je form of aller in the present tense, used to form the near future.

wrong.va: va is the il/elle/on form. The subject is je, so you need vais.
wrong.vas: vas is the tu form. The subject is je, so you need vais.

gaps.rule: Near future — il form of aller
gaps.correct_explain: va is the il form of aller. Mon frère = il.

wrong.vais: vais is the je form. Mon frère = il, so you need va.
wrong.allons: allons is the nous form. Mon frère = il (singular), so you need va.

gaps.rule: Near future — nous form of aller
gaps.correct_explain: allons is the nous form of aller.

wrong.allez: allez is the vous form. The subject is nous, so you need allons.
wrong.vont: vont is the ils/elles form. The subject is nous, so you need allons.

bronze.question: Complete the sentences with the correct preposition for each country

gaps.correct_explain: en is used before feminine countries. La France is feminine.

wrong.au: au is for masculine countries. La France is feminine, so you need en.
wrong.aux: aux is for plural countries. La France is feminine singular, so you need en.

gaps.correct_explain: au is used before masculine countries. Le Canada is masculine.

wrong.en: en is for feminine countries. Le Canada is masculine, so you need au.
wrong.aux: aux is for plural countries. Le Canada is masculine singular, so you need au.

gaps.correct_explain: aux is used before plural countries. Les États-Unis is plural.

wrong.au: au is for masculine singular countries. Les États-Unis is plural, so you need aux.
wrong.en: en is for feminine singular countries. Les États-Unis is plural, so you need aux.

method_card.title: Past Holidays and Experiences
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the perfect tense (le passé composé) for describing past holidays, including avoir and être auxiliaries, DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs, irregular past participles and être agreement.

FrenchEnglish
j'ai visitéI visited
j'ai mangéI ate
j'ai nagéI swam
j'ai jouéI played
j'ai achetéI bought
je suis allé(e)I went
je suis arrivé(e)I arrived
je suis resté(e)I stayed
je suis parti(e)I left
j'ai faitI did/made
j'ai vuI saw
j'ai prisI took
j'ai buI drank

Passé composé with avoir: Subject + avoir (present) + past participle. -er → -é, -ir → -i, -re → -u. Irregulars: faire → fait, voir → vu, prendre → pris, boire → bu, écrire → écrit.

Passé composé with être (DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP): Verbs of movement use être. The past participle must agree with the subject: +e (feminine), +s (masculine plural), +es (feminine plural).

Model: L'année dernière, je suis allé(e) en Espagne. J'ai nagé dans la mer et j'ai visité des musées. C'était fantastique! (Last year, I went to Spain. I swam in the sea and visited museums. It was fantastic!)
steps: Master DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs that take être
Memorise the key irregular past participles (fait, vu, pris, bu, écrit)
Practice past participle agreement with être verbs
Write full paragraphs about past holidays combining avoir and être verbs

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — passé composé tested in every exam series

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'J'ai visité des musées et j'ai mangé de la pizza.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Identify the tense: j'ai + past participle = passé composé (perfect tense).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: j'ai visité = I visited. des musées = museums. j'ai mangé = I ate. de la pizza = pizza.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I visited museums and I ate pizza.

worked_examples.question: How do you decide between avoir and être in the passé composé?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Most verbs use avoir. Check if the verb is a DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verb (mainly movement verbs).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP: Devenir, Revenir, Monter, Rester, Sortir, Venir, Aller, Naître, Descendre, Entrer, Rentrer, Tomber, Retourner, Arriver, Mourir, Partir. These use être.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: With être verbs, the past participle must agree: elle est allée (add -e), ils sont allés (add -s), elles sont allées (add -es).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Use avoir for most verbs. Use être for DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs (movement). With être, the past participle agrees with the subject.

bronze.question: Match the French passé composé forms to the English meaning
Match the irregular past participles to their English meaning
Complete the sentences with the correct auxiliary verb (avoir or être)

gaps.correct_explain: ai is correct because visiter takes avoir in the passé composé.

wrong.suis: suis is the je form of être. Visiter is not a DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verb, so it uses avoir.

gaps.correct_explain: suis is correct because aller is a DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verb and takes être.

wrong.ai: ai is from avoir. Aller is a movement verb (DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP), so it uses être: je suis allé.

gaps.correct_explain: avons is the nous form of avoir. Manger takes avoir.

wrong.sommes: sommes is the nous form of être. Manger uses avoir, not être.
wrong.ont: ont is the ils/elles form of avoir. The subject is nous, so you need avons.

bronze.question: Complete with the correct past participle

gaps.correct_explain: fait is the irregular past participle of faire.

wrong.fais: fais is the present tense. The past participle of faire is fait.
wrong.faire: faire is the infinitive. You need the past participle fait.

gaps.correct_explain: vu is the irregular past participle of voir.

wrong.voir: voir is the infinitive. You need the past participle vu.
wrong.vois: vois is the present tense. The past participle of voir is vu.

gaps.correct_explain: pris is the irregular past participle of prendre.

wrong.prend: prend is the present tense il/elle form. The past participle of prendre is pris.
wrong.prendu: prendu is not a word. Prendre has an irregular past participle: pris.

gaps.correct_explain: allée is correct because elle is feminine, so the past participle of aller (an être verb) must add -e.

wrong.allé: allé is the masculine form. Elle is feminine, so you need to add -e: allée.
wrong.aller: aller is the infinitive. You need the past participle allée (feminine agreement with elle).

gaps.correct_explain: visité is the past participle of visiter (-er → -é). No agreement needed with avoir.

wrong.visitée: visitée would only be correct if la tour Eiffel were a preceding direct object. Here it follows the verb, so no agreement: visité.
wrong.visite: visite is the present tense or noun. The past participle is visité (with accent).

silver.explanation: The second allé refers to ma sœur (feminine). With être verbs, the past participle must agree: allée (add -e for feminine).

method_card.title: Accommodation and Hotels
method_card.content:
This lesson covers hotel booking vocabulary, accommodation types, facilities, meal plans, complaints and the conditional tense for polite requests.

FrenchEnglish
une chambre doublea double room
une chambre individuellea single room
une chambre familialea family room
avec douche / avec bainwith shower / with bath
avec vue sur la merwith a sea view
pour trois nuitsfor three nights
un campinga campsite
une auberge de jeunessea youth hostel
un gîtea holiday cottage
le petit-déjeuner comprisbreakfast included
en demi-pensionhalf board
la climatisationair conditioning
ne marche pasdoesn't work

method_card.title: Countries, Weather and Transport
method_card.content:
This lesson covers weather expressions in different tenses, linking weather to countries and opinions, and a full transport vocabulary revision.

FrenchEnglish
il fait beauit's nice weather
il fait mauvaisit's bad weather
il fait chaudit's hot
il fait froidit's cold
il y a du soleilit's sunny
il y a du ventit's windy
il pleutit's raining
il neigeit's snowing
il y a de l'orageit's stormy
il y a des nuagesit's cloudy
en métroby underground
à motoby motorbike

Weather in the imperfect (past): il faisait (it was — il fait), il pleuvait (it was raining), il neigeait (it was snowing), il y avait (there was — il y a).

Weather in the near future: il va faire beau, il va pleuvoir, il va neiger.

Weather in the simple future: il fera beau, il pleuvra, il neigera, il y aura.

Model: En été, il fait beau en Espagne et il y a du soleil. L'été dernier, il faisait très chaud. Demain, il va faire beau. (In summer, the weather is nice in Spain and it's sunny. Last summer, it was very hot. Tomorrow, it's going to be nice weather.)
steps: Learn the two weather patterns: il fait + adjective and il y a + noun
Master weather in three tenses: present, imperfect (past) and future
Link weather to countries with opinions and connectives for complex sentences
Revise the full range of transport vocabulary with comparisons

worked_examples.question: How do you change weather expressions from present to imperfect (past)?

steps.content: il fait → il faisait (it was). The imperfect stem of faire is fais-, add -ait for il.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: il pleut → il pleuvait. il neige → il neigeait. il y a → il y avait.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Use past time phrases to signal the imperfect: hier (yesterday), l'été dernier (last summer), quand j'étais en vacances (when I was on holiday).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Change il fait → il faisait, il pleut → il pleuvait, il neige → il neigeait, il y a → il y avait. Use past time phrases to signal the tense.

steps.content: 'but' = mais. 'tomorrow' = demain. 'it's going to rain' = near future: il va pleuvoir.

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}
